abstract: This paper discloses an original engineering design sketch created and transmitted via FAX by Yoshimitsu Katayama on 2010-06-12, during the Deepwater Horizon oil spill crisis. The sketch is dated and signed (片山佳光 / Katayama Yoshimitsu), with a contemporary newspaper clipping ('BPのコメ袋作戦失敗') attached as contextual evidence. title: 慣性機関:磁力・電力・慣性力の三重統合による回転機構の設計原理 / Inertia Engine: Design Principles of a Rotational Mechanism Integrating Magnetic Force, Electric Force, and Centrifugal Inertia
abstract: An original motor design concept titled '慣性機関' (Inertia Engine), developed independently by Yoshimitsu Katayama. The design proposes a rotational mechanism integrating three force components: (1) magnetic force (N/S poles), (2) electric force (+/- polarity switching), and (3) centrifugal inertia of the rotating body. Original hand-drawn sketches from the author's personal research notebook are included. The author notes that contemporary wind power generator motor architecture may represent an applied derivation of similar principles. This disclosure establishes priority of conception with permanent timestamp. Key design note: centrifugal force coupling with magnetic/electric force F is identified as the critical mechanism (marked '??' in original sketch). Related concepts: negative gyro application (ネガジャイロ応用), Digitairo application (旧デジタイロへの応用).

title: Location-Based Cryptographic Authentication: A Coordinate-as-Key Protocol for Physical Presence Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cryptographic authentication protocol in which physical geographic coordinates serve as the cryptographic key. Unlike conventional password-based systems, the Coordinate-as-Key (CaK) protocol requires physical presence at a specific GPS location. The key cannot be replicated remotely — it is bound to existence in space, not to knowledge alone. This creates an entirely new category of authentication: Presence-Bound Cryptography (PBC). The concept was conceived and defined at Fukui Prefecture, Japan (35.9606° N, 136.2215° E) on 2026-05-06.
keywords: cryptography, authentication, GPS coordinates, physical presence verification, coordinate-as-key, presence-bound cryptography, geospatial security, location-based authentication

title: Hemispheric Asymmetry in Energy and Signalness of IceCube GOLD Events: An Exploratory Analysis with BRONZE-Class Control Verification
abstract: We report two spatial patterns in the IceCube GOLD alert dataset (N=62, 2019-2026): (1) a statistically significant energy asymmetry between southern and northern sky events (median 349 TeV vs. 202.5 TeV, Mann-Whitney p=0.0189), and (2) an elevated signalness trend in the Leo core zone (RA=120-150 deg), with Leo mean signalness 0.721 vs. 0.558 (p=0.112; not statistically significant). A pre-specified BRONZE-class control analysis (N=118) found neither pattern in BRONZE data (p=0.516 and p=0.729, respectively). This contrast is not readily explained by IceCube directional sensitivity alone, though differences in selection thresholds between GOLD and BRONZE cannot be excluded. Whether the observed patterns reflect distinct astrophysical physics or residual selection systematics cannot be determined from this exploratory analysis. title: Hemispheric Asymmetry in Energy and Signalness of IceCube GOLD Events: An Exploratory Analysis
abstract: We report two independent statistical anomalies in IceCube GOLD-class neutrino alert events (N=54, Rev=1, 2019-2026). First, southern-sky events (Dec<0) show significantly higher median energy than northern-sky events (349 vs. 183 TeV; Spearman rho=-0.328, p=0.0155). Second, Leo core zone events (RA=120-150 deg) show elevated signalness (mean 0.835 vs. 0.565; Mann-Whitney p=0.0186). A simplified Monte Carlo test under isotropic source assumptions suggests both anomalies occurring simultaneously is unlikely (p~0.0002), but this depends on the adopted detector model and should be regarded as preliminary. Whether the asymmetry reflects detector sensitivity effects, source distribution, or both cannot be determined from the present dataset. This paper presents these as exploratory findings requiring pre-registered independent verification. title: Elevated Signalness of IceCube GOLD Events in the Leo Core Zone: A Radio-Loud QSO and Blazar Association Hypothesis
abstract: We report a statistically significant elevation of IceCube GOLD alert signalness in the Leo core zone (RA=120-150 deg) compared to the rest of the sky. The two GOLD events within this zone exhibit mean signalness of 0.835, versus 0.565 for the remaining 52 events (Mann-Whitney p=0.0186; t-test p=0.037). Physical counterpart candidates include 4C 25.26 (radio QSO, Fourth Cambridge Catalogue, 0.164 deg from G2), 4FGL J0927.2+2454 (Fermi blazar, 1.79 deg). Combined with companion paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20000889 (Centaurus/southern-sky result), we propose a North Window / South Pillar duality consistent with AGN jets as dominant neutrino source class.

title: Southern Sky Preference of Ultra-High-Energy IceCube GOLD Events: A Statistical Indication of Centaurus-Direction Neutrino Sources
abstract: We report a statistically significant negative correlation between neutrino energy and declination (Dec) among IceCube GOLD-class alert events (2019–2026). Analyzing 54 GOLD events (Revision 1), we find that higher-energy neutrinos arrive preferentially from lower declinations (southern sky), with Spearman's ρ = −0.328 (p = 0.0155). Events with Dec < 0° show a mean energy of 1,036 TeV compared to 278 TeV for Dec ≥ 0° events (Mann-Whitney U test, p = 0.0362; ratio 3.73×). After correcting for IceCube's reduced sensitivity in the southern sky, the estimated true flux ratio reaches 10.2×. The southern sky direction is consistent with Centaurus A (NGC 5128, Dec = −43.0°), the nearest active galactic nucleus and a well-established ultra-high-energy cosmic ray candidate source. We conclude that the current non-detection of IceCube alerts from Cen A is a consequence of detector geometry rather than source absence. This prediction is testable by KM3NeT and IceCube-Gen2.
keywords: IceCube, neutrino, Centaurus A, NGC 5128, high-energy astrophysics, southern sky, AGN, UHECR, multimessenger astronomy, statistical analysis

title: A Complete X-ray Spectral Survey of ISP BL Lac Objects in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Confidence Catalog: Evidence for a Rare Spectral Hardening Class
abstract: We present the first complete X-ray spectral survey of all 347 ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-confidence catalog using archival Swift-XRT data. Of 347 targets, 242 had sufficient data for analysis, yielding 220 Class-S (spectral softening) and 14 Class-H (spectral hardening) objects. Only one object — 1WGA J0506.6-0857 — exhibits statistically significant spectral hardening (p=0.037, β=2.11, r=0.90). The rarity of Class-H objects (0.4% statistically significant) is quantitatively consistent with the ΔP_Ma Hypothesis, which predicts that spectral hardening arises from resonant vacuum energy amplification at cosmic Ma (間) boundaries. This catalog constitutes the first population-level X-ray spectral baseline for ISP BL Lacs and identifies 1WGA J0506.6-0857 as the highest-priority new IceCube multi-messenger follow-up target.
keywords: ISP BL Lac, blazar, X-ray spectroscopy, Swift-XRT, 4LAC-DR3, spectral hardening, multi-messenger astronomy, IceCube, TXS 0506+056, ΔP_Ma hypothesis
